citing_sentences: Figure 8 shows a grouping of GPUs for hybrid model and data parallelism.
Two or more GPUs within the same server form model parallel groups (for example GPUs 1 to 8 in Figure 8), and contain one instance of the model distributed across these GPUs.

GPUs with the same position in each of the model parallel groups (for example GPUs 1, 9, …, 505 in Figure 8) form data parallel groups so that all GPUs within a data parallel group hold the same model parameters.

abstract: Recent work in language modeling demonstrates that training large transformer models advances the state of the art in Natural Language Processing applications. However, very large models can be quite difficult to train due to memory constraints. In this work, we present our techniques for training very large transformer models and implement a simple, efficient intra-layer model parallel approach that enables training transformer models with billions of parameters. Our approach does not require a new compiler or library changes, is orthogonal and complimentary to pipeline model parallelism, and can be fully implemented with the insertion of a few communication operations in native PyTorch. We illustrate this approach by converging transformer based models up to 8.3 billion parameters using 512 GPUs. We sustain 15.1 PetaFLOPs across the entire application with 76% scaling efficiency when compared to a strong single GPU baseline that sustains 39 TeraFLOPs, which is 30% of peak FLOPs. To demonstrate that large language models can further advance the state of the art (SOTA), we train an 8.3 billion parameter transformer language model similar to GPT-2 and a 3.9 billion parameter model similar to BERT. We show that careful attention to the placement of layer normalization in BERT-like models is critical to achieving increased performance as the model size grows. Using the GPT-2 model we achieve SOTA results on the WikiText103 (10.8 compared to SOTA perplexity of 15.8) and LAMBADA (66.5% compared to SOTA accuracy of 63.2%) datasets. Our BERT model achieves SOTA results on the RACE dataset (90.9% compared to SOTA accuracy of 89.4%).

sections.body: The section introduces an intra-layer model parallel approach implemented in PyTorch with no custom compiler. A 1.2 billion parameter model on a single NVIDIA V100 32GB GPU sustains 39 TeraFLOPs, which is 30% of theoretical peak. Scaling to 8.3 billion parameters on 512 GPUs with 8-way model parallelism sustains up to 15.1 PetaFLOPs, a 76% scaling efficiency relative to the single GPU case. The authors also report that the existing BERT architecture degrades as size grows, and that rearranging layer normalization and residual connections lets downstream development-set results improve monotonically with size. Test-set SOTA is reported on WikiText103, LAMBADA and RACE.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Megatron-LM trains transformers up to 8.3 billion parameters with intra-layer model parallelism, reaching 76% scaling efficiency on 512 GPUs.

sections.body: The section reviews pretraining history, transformer language models, and data and model parallelism. It states that GPipe and Mesh-TensorFlow require rewriting models or relying on custom compilers and frameworks still under development. It notes that GPipe's pipeline approach suffers from pipeline bubbles or optimizer changes that impact accuracy. The authors state their approach exploits parallelism in the transformer's attention heads and is inserted into existing PyTorch transformer implementations by adding a few simple primitives. Figure 2 gives a schematic of the transformer architecture used, with GeLU nonlinearities and layer normalization applied to the input of the attention and feed forward layers.
sections.heading: Background and Challenges
sections.headline: Existing model parallel methods need custom compilers or pipeline changes, so the authors modify only a PyTorch transformer.

sections.body: The MLP first GEMM is split column-wise so GeLU applies independently to each partition, and the second GEMM is split row-wise, requiring one all-reduce in the forward pass and one in the backward pass. Self-attention partitions the key, query and value GEMMs column-wise by attention head, so each head's matmul runs locally on one GPU. The output embedding is fused with cross-entropy loss, so only scalar losses rather than logits are communicated. Layer normalization parameters and dropout are duplicated on each GPU instead of being broadcast. The section describes the design in words and states it needs no compiler and is complementary to pipeline parallelism.
sections.heading: Model Parallel Transformers
sections.headline: The MLP and attention blocks are split across GPUs so each transformer layer needs only four all-reduce operations.

sections.body: The training corpus combines Wikipedia, CC-Stories, RealNews and OpenWebtext, with WikiText103 test-set Wikipedia articles removed to prevent leakage. BooksCorpus is included for BERT but excluded for GPT-2 because it overlaps with LAMBADA. Documents under 128 tokens are filtered out, and locality-sensitive hashing removes content with a Jaccard similarity greater than 0.7, leaving 174 GB of text. GPT-2 uses sequences of 1024 subword units, batch size 512, 300k iterations, and a learning rate of 1.5e-4 with cosine decay. BERT uses batch size 1024, learning rate 1.0e-4, and a vocabulary of 30,522, with sentence order prediction in place of next sentence prediction.
sections.heading: Setup
sections.headline: GPT-2 and BERT models train on an aggregated 174 GB deduplicated corpus with fixed optimizer and learning-rate schedules.

sections.body: The scaling study uses four GPT-2 configurations from 1.2 billion to 8.3 billion parameters, reporting 77% of linear scaling for 8-way model parallelism and 74% for 512 GPUs with data parallelism. Table 2 gives GPT-2 configurations with 355M, 2.5B and 8.3B parameters, and the 8.3B model reaches a validation perplexity of 9.27. On zero-shot evaluation, the 8.3B model scores 10.81 perplexity on WikiText103 against a previous SOTA of 15.79, and 66.51% accuracy on LAMBADA against 63.24%. Table 5 reports BERT results, with the 3.9B model reaching SOTA RACE test-set results. The authors note that test-set overlap with training data is at most 10.8% for WikiText103 and 1.4% for LAMBADA.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Model parallel scaling reaches 77% of linear scaling at 8.3 billion parameters, and GPT-2 and BERT results set new SOTA marks.

sections.body: The conclusion restates that the approach trains transformers up to 8.3 billion parameters on 512 NVIDIA V100 GPUs with 8-way model parallelism, sustaining up to 15.1 PetaFLOPs. It repeats that careful placement of layer normalization is critical for BERT-like models as size grows, and that new SOTA results are set on WikiText103, LAMBADA and RACE. The authors state that a model above 16 billion parameters would exceed the memory of 16 GPUs in a DGX-2H box, and suggest hybrid intra-layer and inter-layer parallelism for such models. Listed future work includes memory-efficient optimizers, pretraining other model families, harder downstream tasks, and knowledge distillation.
sections.heading: Conclusion and Future Work
sections.headline: The authors conclude that intra-layer parallelism scales to 8.3 billion parameters and suggest hybrid parallelism for larger models.

sections.body: Appendix A gives finetuning batch sizes, learning rates and epochs for MNLI, QQP, SQuAD and RACE at 336M, 1.3B and 3.8B. Appendix B describes grouping GPUs into model and data parallel groups, with 8 GPUs per model parallel group and 64-way data parallelism for the 8.3 billion parameter model, and seeding dropout differently inside and outside model parallel regions. Appendix C shows generated text samples. Appendix D reports how attention head count affects scaling efficiency, with 82% for 16 heads and 77% for 32 heads, and strong scaling speedups of 1.64 with two GPUs. Appendix E defines WikiText103 perplexity with overlapping evaluation using an overlap of 32 and the LAMBADA cloze protocol.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists BERT finetuning hyperparameters, hybrid parallelism and random number details, text samples, evaluation methodology, and strong scaling results.
